native_result.query: What types of plant introductions were influenced by urban land use?
native_result.HypoA: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.
native_result.HypoB: Urban land use in Barcelona province was associated with unintentional plant introductions (accidental arrivals via seed contamination, trade and tourism) and, secondarily and more weakly, with gardening (ornamental) introductions, while agriculture/forestry introductions were not influenced by urban land. Evidence: per-pathway presence/absence logistic models across 632 plots (adjusted for cropland, elevation, road/stream distance, climate, radiation) show Unintentional presence odds rise ~26x per unit urban cover in the 1-km buffer (p<0.0001, also p<0.0001 for 1956-2009 urbanization, ~1.4x per +10pp), Gardening follows the same positive direction but weaker (OR 2.5, p=0.15), AgriForest shows no urban association (OR=0.2, p=0.3); the Unintentional-vs-AgriForest slope contrast is significant (z=2.9, p=0.004) and is replicated at the 50-m buffer. Temporally, Gardening rose to 75.2% of 1985-2019 introductions (chi2=230, p<0.0001) - the urbanization era - while AgriForest collapsed, corroborating which pathway types track urban land. Association, not causation.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspected all four files: plot file (632x37, no missing, n.total=sum of pathway counts, 441/632 zero plots) is the only file pairing pathway counts with urban land; species traits/phylogeny cannot join plots (no species IDs in plot file). 2) Primary unit=632 plots; outcomes=presence of n.unint/n.gard/n.agfo/n.total; exposures=urban cover 2009 and delta-urban 1956-2009 (1000m primary, 50m sensitivity); controls=cropland, elevation, road/stream distance, temperature, rainfall, radiation (z-standardized); habitat excluded (proxy/exposure bad-control, reported diagnostically via Firth). 3) Single-exposure marginal adjusted logistic models per pathway (all converged), effect sizes with CIs, per-10pp ORs, cross-pathway slope contrasts (unint vs agfo, gard vs agfo, unint vs gard). 4) Zero-inflation handled via logistic primary; negative-binomial counts corroborate direction; zero fraction vs NB expectation reported. 5) Temporal corroboration via period x pathway chi-square and standardized residuals. 6) Synthesized single natural-language hypothesis naming the pathway types influenced by urban land use.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Urban land use reduced invasion by gardening plants over unintentionally introduced ones.

sub_hypo.text: Urban land use was positively associated with unintentional plant introductions in Barcelona province, more weakly associated with gardening introductions, and not significantly associated with agriculture/forestry introductions. These are associations, not causal effects.
sub_hypo.context: 632 plots in Barcelona province; pathway-specific presence/absence logistic models using 2009 urban cover and change in urban cover from 1956 to 2009 as separate exposures, primarily within 1-km buffers, with 50-m sensitivity analyses. Models adjusted for cropland, elevation, road and stream distances, temperature, rainfall, and radiation; habitat was excluded from primary models.
sub_hypo.relations: Counts were converted to presence/absence. Unintentional introduction presence odds increased approximately 26-fold per unit of urban cover within 1 km (p<0.0001); urbanization, calculated as 2009 minus 1956 urban cover, was also positively associated (p<0.0001; approximately 1.4-fold odds per 10-percentage-point increase). Gardening had a weaker positive association (OR=2.5, p=0.15), whereas agriculture/forestry had no significant urban association (OR=0.2, p=0.3). The unintentional-versus-agriculture/forestry slope contrast was significant (z=2.9, p=0.004) and replicated within 50-m buffers. Negative-binomial count models corroborated the direction.

sub_hypo.text: During the urbanization era, gardening introductions increased to dominate recent non-native plant introductions, while agriculture/forestry introductions collapsed, providing temporal corroboration of pathway-specific associations with urban land.
sub_hypo.context: Temporal introduction-pathway data for non-native flora in Catalonia, particularly the 1985–2019 introduction period.
sub_hypo.relations: Introduction frequencies varied by period and pathway: gardening accounted for 75.2% of introductions in 1985–2019, while agriculture/forestry introductions collapsed. The period-by-pathway chi-square analysis yielded chi2=230, p<0.0001. This temporal pattern provides corroboration, not causal evidence, for the urban-land associations.
